reasoning:
The reproduction re-runs exactly (one correction: it needs GET /api/data, not ?view=app, which carries no playersArray and returns an empty pool). The defect is real and unfixed at HEAD: src/trade/suggestions.py:698 `_apply_board_top_n_filter` is a single global cut on `board_rank` with no per-family handling, so 0 of 96 DBs survive while src/trade/finder.py:579-583 documents this exact failure mode ('a single global top-150 removes every IDP player (WS-J F-3)') and fixes it per-market. The in-code comment at suggestions.py:229-238 asserting the blended board 'answers directly and for every asset class, including IDP' is contradicted by its own output. needPositions contains 'DB' for 12/12 teams; the badge markup at frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:1097-1103 renders it as a negative Badge. All confirmed.

P0 fails three of the protocol's own tests, so this is rescoped to P1, not overturned:
(1) 'no warning shown' is false. The SAME panel, 20 lines above the badge (trade-sections.jsx:1074-1081), renders `{totalSuggestions} suggestions · {rosterMatched}/{rosterCount} matched` — '6 suggestions · 16/57 matched' for Jason, '3/44' for jstuedle. That is a rendered disclosure that the analysis covers a minority of the roster. It does not name the DB blind spot, which is why the finding survives at all, but it defeats the P0 'no warning' clause.
(2) 'a user acts on a wrong number' is not met. Every number a trade is actually priced on is correct — the sellHigh/buyLow cards read `rankDerivedValue` and their arithmetic is untouched. The wrong output is an advisory label. Furthermore src/trade/suggestions.py:281 documents `starter_counts` as `# above-replacement count`, not a raw roster count. Under the engine's own definition 'you have zero above-replacement DBs' is literally TRUE for all 12 teams. The finding's inferential step — from 'no DB in pool' to 'the engine reports a shortage that does not exist' — silently substitutes raw-count semantics the code never claimed. What is genuinely defective is narrower and still worth fixing: because 'above replacement' is operationalised as 'top-150 OVERALL on a scale where DB peaks at 3159 against a board max of 9988', the DB need is structurally permanent, identical for every team, and unsatisfiable by the engine that raised it — a signal that can never turn off carries no information. Note the same is largely true of DL (need for 10/12) and LB (11/12), which the finding treats as working.
(3) blastRadius playersAffected:139 is not derivable from anything I could recount. The pool holds 96 DBs and excludes all 96; total IDP excluded is 279 (DL 115-7=108, LB 82-7=75, DB 96-0=96). 139 matches neither.
Minor: numericProof.startingSlots=21 is wrong — live metadata.starterNeeds sums to 20, so the IDP lineup share is 9/20 = 45.0%, not 42.86%. Direction and conclusion unchanged.

correctedBlastRadius.playersAffectedNote: 96 DBs, 100% excluded from the suggestion pool; 279 IDP rows excluded in total (DL 108 + LB 75 + DB 96) out of an 812-row pool

whatWouldSettleIt: Change _apply_board_top_n_filter to cut per position family (mirroring finder.py's market_groups at finder.py:583-599) and re-run the 12-roster sweep: DB should enter the pool and needPositions should stop containing 'DB' for teams that roster startable DBs. Separately, decide the semantics question the finding papers over — if starter_counts is meant to stay an above-replacement count, the fix is to suppress or footnote needPositions for any family with zero pool coverage, not to switch it to a raw roster count.

reasoning:
The reproduction runs and produces exactly the stated output. The mechanism is confirmed at HEAD: server.py:11748 passes `_scrape_status_payload()`, which (server.py:1290-1304) returns `dict(scrape_status)` plus stall_threshold_sec / run_timeout_sec / status_summary and nothing else; `scrape_success_rate_24h` is written in exactly one place, server.py:4352, inside `get_status()`, and its value is the dict returned by `_scrape_success_rate_24h()` (server.py:1104-1124). src/api/ops_alerts.py:46-52 short-circuits on both shapes. The alert is dead. That much is upheld.

Rescoped on three counts.
(1) Novelty is misstated. priorFinding.note claims 'the prior finding named only the missing key' and presents the float(dict) TypeError as a 'second, independent kill' discovered here. PRIOR-A07-F03 already states verbatim: 'Even if the key were added, get_status stamps it as a dict and float(dict) raises TypeError, which the except clause swallows into another None' — and even carries the same `float({'total':10,...})` reproduction. This is a clean confirmation, not an extension.
(2) userImpact ('the operator is not told when more than half the scheduled scrapes fail... every alert channel stays quiet') is false. Four other live channels cover the same condition: server.py:2516 sends an email on EVERY scrape exception ('Scrape failed: {type}'); server.py:2369 emails on a blocked partial scrape; the ops sweep's own `_check_data_freshness` IS correctly wired (server.py:11749-11762, threshold 3x SCRAPE_INTERVAL_HOURS) and fires when sustained failure ages the board — the finding's own whatWorks concedes this; and .github/workflows/health-check.yml:78-90 reads /api/status's dict correctly and emits ::warning when rate < 0.5. What is dead is one redundant aggregate-rate alert, not the failure signal.
(3) blastRadius is inflated. playersAffected:1092 is unfounded — no player value is affected by a dead alert. routesAffected:2 counts /api/status, which is not defective: it publishes a well-formed dict that its actual consumer (health-check.yml) parses correctly. Only the ops leg of /api/signal-alerts/run is affected.
P1 implies operator-visible loss of coverage; with four surviving channels this is a redundancy gap, so P2.
whatWouldSettleIt: Apply the stated repair (pass {**_scrape_status_payload(), 'scrape_success_rate_24h': _scrape_success_rate_24h().get('rate')} at server.py:11748) and assert the ops sweep returns a scrape_failure alert when scrape_history holds >50% failures inside 24h. The severity question is settled by whether an operator with ALERT_ENABLED gets any email at all during a sustained scrape outage — server.py:2516 says they do.

reasoning:
The observation reproduces verbatim on the correct topology (request interception, not plain :3000). MoversPanel.jsx:154-164 reads only `data.risers` / `data.fallers` and builds its subtitle from local `windowDays` state; `window`, `windowRequested` and `historyDepthDays` are never referenced anywhere in the file. The backend docstring at server.py:3385-3391 explicitly created `window` to stop exactly this mislabel ('reporting the request in that case labelled a 2-day delta "90 days"'). MoversPanel is rendered on `/` via frontend/app/page.jsx:17 -> TerminalLayout.jsx:76, so the page claim is right. Genuine, unfixed frontend defect. But four corrections force a rescope:

(1) The MarketTicker half is REFUTED. The finding says 'MarketTicker.jsx:126 compounds it'. It does not — MarketTicker never touches /api/movers or rank_history. frontend/lib/market-movers.js:1-22 states it reads the contract's per-row `rankChange` 'verbatim rather than recomputing from rank_history', and that field is populated on the live contract: 694 ints, 572 of them nonzero. The 'Market quiet in my roster' string I captured is produced because NO team was selected (the page simultaneously renders 'Pick your team' / 'Pick a team to see allocation'), i.e. an empty roster scope — a different defect with a different cause, not this one.

(2) The alarming state is container-conditional. `historyDepthDays: 0 / asOf: null` holds because `data/rank_history.jsonl` does not exist in this container (ls: No such file or directory) — the audit harness suppresses the scrape that writes it. In production the file exists; the backend docstring says it 'is only a few days deep today'. So the specific reading the userImpact turns on ('the user concludes the dynasty market has been flat') is not the production state. What IS live in production is the narrower and durable defect: whenever `window < windowRequested` — which the backend says is the normal case — the subtitle labels an N-day delta with the requested span. That is a mislabel, not a fabricated market fact.

(3) The title and userImpact both say the subtitle reads 'Rank deltas vs. 30d ago'. Default state is `useState(14)` (MoversPanel.jsx:127) and the rendered page says '14d ago'; the finding's own reproduction.actual also says 14d. The 30d wording only appears after a user clicks the 30d segment. Self-inconsistent.

(4) blastRadius playersAffected:1092 is unfounded — no player is mispriced; the panel shows at most 16 rows (limit=8 per side) and every delta it would show is a real one.

Display-layer mislabel with no wrong value acted upon => P2.
whatWouldSettleIt: Seed data/rank_history.jsonl with 3 days of snapshots and request window=30. If the panel still prints 'Rank deltas vs. 30d ago' over a 3-day delta, the production-live half of this finding is proven independent of the harness. Conversely, confirming MarketTicker with a team selected and >=3 nonzero rankChange rows on that roster settles that its 'Market quiet' string is unrelated to rank history.
